blocks.text: You can manage your Microsoft Azure decoys from the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal. All decoys created from the Deception Admin Portal are tabulated under their respective decoy category tabs. Each table shows the details associated with each decoy in the category and also shows its deployment status. You can also edit or delete decoys by using the respective options from the decoys table.

At the time of integration, Zscaler Deception deploys a health check function on Azure. This function periodically checks all decoy resources deployed on Azure and updates their status to the Deception Admin Portal every 15 minutes. You can check the deployment status indicated by the icon next to the name of the decoy in the decoys table. The following icons are used to show the status of the decoys:

blocks.item: – Indicates a deployed state.

– Indicates an inactive state. This means the decoy no longer exists on Azure or one of its properties used to reference does not exist. This happens when the decoy or its resources are manipulated directly from Azure.

– Indicates a pending deployment state. This means that the decoy has been created or modified in the Deception Admin Portal, but the deployment script to propagate changes to the Azure Cloud has not been initiated.

– Indicates a pending deletion state. This means that the decoy has been deleted from the Deception Admin Portal, but the deployment script to propagate changes to the Azure Cloud has not been initiated.

blocks.text: You can edit or delete the Azure decoys that you configured in the Deception Admin Portal. Such changes made to the Azure decoys in the Deception Admin Portall are propagated to the Azure Cloud only after running the deployment script on the Azure Cloud Shell.
Obtain the PowerShell command using one of the following methods:

blocks.item: Automated Download Method
Manual Download Method

blocks.text: This only applies to the Cloud Shell-based deployment.

blocks.item: Go to Deceive > Cloud Deception > Azure.
Select the relevant decoy category tab. For example, if you want to edit a user decoy, select the User tab.
Make sure that the decoy you want to edit is in the Not Deployed state, and then click the Edit icon.
See image.
Modify the decoy details as per your requirements.
Click Save.
Deploy the changes based on the method used to configure the integration between Azure and Deception:
Terraform-based deployment
On the Cloud Deception - Azure page, go to Settings.
Locate the Azure account you added, and click the Download icon in the Actions column.
See image.
In the Terraform Deployment Steps window, click Download to download the necessary files.
See image.
A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the azure-decoys.tf.json file in a text editor.
Locate the backend block in the azure-decoys.tf.json file. Add your back-end details and save the file.
The following example shows a backend block of an Azure blob storage-based Terraform back end:

{ "terraform": { "backend": { "azurerm": { "resource_group_name": "your-tfstate-rg", "storage_account_name": "yourtfstatestorageacct", "container_name": "tfstate", "key": "deception/terraform.tfstate" } } } }
Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same Azure account.
In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and run the following command to create a new workspace:
terraform init && terraform workspace new <workspace_name>
Run the following command to deploy resources:
terraform apply
Review the plan, and confirm it by entering Yes when prompted.
The necessary resources are deployed.
Run the following command to download the details of the state as a JSON file.
terraform output -json decoys_output > deployment-output.json
A JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
On the Cloud Deception - Azure page, go to Settings, locate the Azure account you added, and click the Upload icon in the Actions column.
See image.
Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Deception Admin Portal.
Cloud Shell-based deployment
Sign in to the Azure Portal as a Cloud Device Administrator or Global Administrator.
Launch Cloud Shell by clicking the Cloud Shell icon on the top navigation bar.
See image.
The Cloud Shell window appears.
In the Cloud Shell window:
Set your shell environment to PowerShell.
Run the deployment script using the command obtained via the automated download method or manual download method.
Enter the option to deploy the preferred decoy and press Enter.
See image.

blocks.text: Upon successful execution, the changes are propagated to the Azure Cloud.
